Allow extra time for elevation gain and rough ground — mapped distances are rarely flat walking pace.
Pack a wind layer and rain shell even on fair days; exposed ridges cool down fast.
Take a map you can read offline and note where phone signal drops out.
Check whether the trail crosses private land, parks with entry fees, or seasonal wildlife closures.
Carry more water than you think you need on warm days; refill plans can fall through.
Leave a rough itinerary with someone who is not on the hike, including your expected return.
In alpine terrain, turn back if weather worsens — ridges are not the place to wait it out.
Stick to marked paths where they exist to reduce erosion and avoid cliff edges not visible on maps.
